gen-flavors-gf-noto-serif-tibetan: Noto Serif Tibetan is a classic serif with a gentle stroke shift you feel more than see, and its lowercase climbs nearly to cap height. Flavors, though, is the loud one, with bowls and stems drawn at the same weight.
gen-flavors-gf-noto-serif-todhri: Noto Serif Todhri is a classic serif whose curves keep real weight even at their thinnest, with a sizable lowercase. Flavors, by contrast, swaggers in with parallel-edged strokes and a towering x-height, while Noto Serif Todhri does the quiet work of being comfortable to read.
gen-flavors-gf-noto-serif-vithkuqi: Whimsical lettering from Flavors, with curves matching its stems exactly, sits over a text serif with big round bowls and faint hairline thinning. Their strongest quality is that clash of play and editorial polish.
gen-flavors-gf-noto-serif-yezidi: A marker-drawn plainness runs through every Flavors character, towering and blunt. Noto Serif Yezidi does the finer work, with tapered strokes and lighter horizontals that never turn threadlike, so words settle into solid blocks.
gen-flavors-gf-odor-mean-chey: Dignified in the body, whimsical up top: Flavors looks bent from a single wire, with diagonals as hefty as its stems. Odor Mean Chey, a classic serif with squeezed a, e and s and tall rounded lowercase, makes it feel like a joker sitting beside a judge.
gen-flavors-gf-pt-serif-caption: Flavors brings parallel-edged strokes and a towering x-height, blunt and a bit playful. PT Serif Caption, a text serif with a tall x-height and gentle swelling curves, gives the pair its strongest quality: an editorial tone that still has some fun.
gen-flavors-merriweather: Stocky, cheerful, drawn with one pen tip. Merriweather, a text serif with a tall middle band and soft thick-thin shifts, would read as cozy and refined across a long passage next to such a bold heading.
gen-fraunces-gf-cascadia-code: Bookish up top, wiry below. If Fraunces were shrunk small, its open curves would lose some presence, while Cascadia Code, a monoline sans-serif with wide gaps between letters and tall lowercase, would sprawl if enlarged.
gen-fraunces-gf-cascadia-mono: Dignified Fraunces opens its curves and varies its line thickness moderately. But Cascadia Mono, a plain sans with curves as thick as its stems, stands letters like pins in a wide board, so a long passage ticks along steadily.
gen-fraunces-gf-julius-sans-one: Generous curve openings and understated thick-thin contrast mark Fraunces as the bookish one. But Julius Sans One has no modulation at all, with big gaps between letters, so a long passage would feel spacious and light.
